Apply the owner's review notes to the edit in this folder with the video-use skill, and finish it again as a live preview in edit/preview/.

Job: client "מאפיית הצפון", job "פרומו לסוף השבוע". The footage folder is the current working directory; treat its files as read-only and write everything to ./edit/.

Footage quality. Whatever the brief says, choose and trim the footage by these three rules:
- Stutters and misspeaks: read the word-level transcript and cut false starts, repeated words, trailing-off sentences and flubbed lines. When a line is said more than once, keep the cleanest take, not the first.
- Photos: check each photo’s resolution and look at it for blur and noise. Use a low-quality photo only as a last resort, when no video or better photo covers that beat.
- Shaky footage: avoid it. Check stability by looking at frames spread through each clip. When a clip shakes at the start and then settles, start it where it settles; use only its most stable stretch. Take a shaky clip only when nothing steadier covers the beat, and say so in project.md.
Self-eval before the final render: no stutter or misspoken line, no shaky stretch and no weak photo left in the cut, unless it was the last resort.

If edit/brief.md exists, read it before anything else (edit/brief.json is the same brief as data). It was written from the client’s instructions and the owner’s note:
- Where it says something, follow it over the §0 defaults table and over your own taste. Where it says nothing, use the defaults.
- Cut only the files it lists as footage. Use music, logo and reference files for what they are. Never put an instructions file (voice note, chat, screenshot) in the video.
- Keep every must-include item and check each one in self-eval before the final render. Nothing on the must-avoid list may appear.
- Use on-screen text word for word.
- Start project.md’s Assumptions line with the brief’s assumptions.
- A Series section, when there is one, is the format this job repeats: follow it exactly. The Client style section at the end is the client’s house style. The brief above them wins where they disagree, and the series wins over the style.

This is review round 1. The owner watched the preview in edit/preview/ and wrote their notes in edit/review/round-1.md. Each note is pinned to a moment on the preview's timeline (m:ss.s). A voice note comes with its transcript; its audio file is listed next to it in case the transcript is missing or the tone matters.
- Load the skill, then read edit/review/round-1.md, edit/project.md and the composition in edit/preview/ before anything else.
- Do not transcribe the footage again and do not start over: change the existing edit.
- Do what each note asks and nothing else. Every other decision (cuts, look, graphics, captions, music) stays as it is.
- Music: keep the pick and edit/preview/music.mp3 as they are, with the composition playing music.mp3 under its volume lane; when the cut changes, move the lane with it (the lift where the music plays alone, the ducking under speech, the ramp before the end card's words). Only the music script, node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs", writes edit/music/ and edit/preview/music.mp3: never change them yourself, and never make or fetch music any other way. Each call takes `"<edit dir>"`, the absolute path of ./edit/ in double quotes, runs as a Bash command of its own, and prints one JSON line that says whether it worked.
- When the notes change the cut's length or the moments the music was made for (the drop, the end card), and edit/music/music.json says it was made ("source": "made"): once the new cut is fixed, update edit/music/plan.json to it (sections on the new cut's boundaries, in whole ms, 3000 to 120000 ms each, adding up to lengthMs, the new duration in ms; describe says it fits the new cut, for example "Fitted to the new 0:42 cut. Builds to a big drop at 0:18 and lands on the logo at 0:38."). Keep the plan's rules: each section's name is one or two plain words ("Build", "Drop", "Logo"), since the script sends it as "[Name]" and other words can be sung; styles and avoid hold only short style tags; and the section right before a drop has the drop's weight in its avoid ("kick drum", "sub bass", "full drums"). Then, unless the pick is off ("picked": "off"), run `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" make "<edit dir>" --by revise` with a Bash timeout of 600000 ms, check its drop (below), and line the cuts up with the kept take's beats and its drop, keeping the length.
- Music that was not asked for: when edit/music/music.json says "source": "none" with the reason "Music was not asked for.", nothing was made on purpose and a revise makes no music, unless a note asks for some (a note that asks for music, or says how music should sound, is "a note that asks for music when there is none yet" in the next line; a note that asks for another song is under it). When the notes change the cut's length or the moments the music would be made for, update edit/music/plan.json to the new cut (the plan rules above) and run `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" none "<edit dir>" "Music was not asked for." --plan` again, so Make music in Review fits the new cut and the silence at edit/preview/music.mp3 has its length; keep the composition's music element and volume lane, and move the lane with the cut as above.
- A note about the music itself: "no music" is `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" pick "<edit dir>" off`; a version it names ("go back to v1") is `pick "<edit dir>" v1`; how it should sound ("calmer", "darker, more drums", "different music") is `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" make "<edit dir>" --again --ask "<what the note asks of the music, in English, at most 200 characters>" --by revise` (leave out --again when this round also updated plan.json, so one make fits both); how loud it is, is the lane's job, not a new version (where the music plays alone, the lane can lift it by up to +12 dB). A note that asks for music when there is none yet: write plan.json for the cut if it is missing (lengthMs, styles, avoid, sections of name, ms, styles and avoid, and describe; always instrumental, with the plan's rules above), run make with --by revise, check its drop (below), and play music.mp3 in the composition under a volume lane.
- A note that asks for another song ("Use [title] by [artist] instead.", "Use the song from [link] instead.", "Use a trending song that fits the cut.") is not about how the music sounds, so make no music for it. Once the round's cut is fixed, set lengthMs in edit/music/plan.json to its length in ms (write the plan for the cut first if it is missing, as for a note that asks for music where there is none), then get the song with a Bash timeout of 600000 ms: `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" song "<edit dir>" --title "<title>" --artist "<artist>" --from note --by you`; for a link, `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" song "<edit dir>" --link "<link>" --from note --by you`; for a trending song, `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" song "<edit dir>" --trending --from trending --by you`, adding `--niche "#a #b #c"` (2 to 4 hashtags for what the video shows) only when the client's style has no "Reels niche:" line. On {"ok":true,…} edit/preview/music.mp3 is the new song's part and the line gives its `part` ({startMs, endMs, how}) and `beats` (ms from the part's start): line the cuts up with those beats and the drop's cut with the part's measured drop, keeping the length (no drop check, no make), duck the song under speech as the first pass does (harder, or the speech over an instrumental stretch, where it sings over someone talking), and say in that note's line which song you used and what you moved. On {"ok":false,…} the music stays as it was: say so, and why, in that note's line of the round. One song call per note.
- A note about where the song's words come in against the picture ("music only at first, then the lyrics when the images start", "start with the instrumental intro", "the lyrics on the beat when the photo opens") is about which part of the song plays, not about the cuts: moving the cuts or the music's start inside the part you have does not answer it. Set lengthMs in edit/music/plan.json to the cut's length and get the same song again with a Bash timeout of 600000 ms (the song is kept, nothing is downloaded again): the song call of the note above for the song in edit/music/music.json (its title and artist, or its link), `--from note --by you`, plus `--lyrics-at <ms>`: the time in the cut where the words should start, in ms (the moment in the note, or the one the brief names). The script cuts the part to start that long before the song's first word, so the song's own intro is the lead-in; play edit/preview/music.mp3 from the cut's first frame and never delay or silence its start. The line's `lyricsMs` is where the first word is heard in the part; if it is smaller than the ms asked, the song has a shorter intro: start the music that much later in the cut and say so. Put the cut at that moment on the beat nearest `lyricsMs` when that beat is within 80 ms of it, else keep it where it is; line the other cuts up on the line's `beats` (where they wander under the singing, count whole beats at the line's `bpm` from the nearest of its `downbeats`), and say in that note's line which part of the song now plays and where its words start. On {"ok":false,…} the music stays as it was: say so, and why, in that note's line of the round.
- A note that gives a moment of the song to start from ("start the song at 0:37", "begin at 1:05 of the song") is about which part of the song plays, not about the cuts: moving the cuts or the music's start inside the part you have does not answer it. Set lengthMs in edit/music/plan.json to the cut's length and get the same song again with a Bash timeout of 600000 ms (the song is kept, nothing is downloaded again): the song call of the note above for the song in edit/music/music.json (its title and artist, or its link), `--from note --by you`, plus `--start-ms <ms>`: that moment in the song, in ms (0:37 is 37000). The part starts exactly there; play edit/preview/music.mp3 from the cut's first frame and never delay or silence its start. Line the cuts up on the line's `beats` (where they wander under the singing, count whole beats at the line's `bpm` from the nearest of its `downbeats`), and say in that note's line which part of the song now plays. If the line's note says the part starts earlier than asked, say so there too. On {"ok":false,…} the music stays as it was: say so, and why, in that note's line of the round.
- A note about the song's timing ("start the song at the chorus", "later drop") changes where the cuts sit on the same song: line them up with other beats of the part you already have (its start and end are in edit/music/music.json), don't get the song again, and say in that note's line that you moved the cuts and the part itself stays as it is. A note that gives the time in the song (m:ss) is the one above instead.
- When the notes change the cut's length and edit/music/music.json says the pick is the song ("picked": "song"), its part was cut for the old length: set lengthMs in edit/music/plan.json to the new length and run the song command again for the same song (its title, artist or link are in the record) with the same options, then line the cuts up with the new beats.
- Checking the drop, after a make for a new cut or for music where there was none: measure the track with `npx hyperframes audio "<edit dir>/preview/music.mp3" --only beats,downbeats,bpm,sections --json`; its drop is the measured section change nearest plan.json's drop. If it landed more than one beat from it (60 / BPM seconds), run `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" make "<edit dir>" --again --by revise` once (with the first make's --ask and its words, if it had them) and measure that take too. The make picks its new version; if the earlier take's drop was closer, put that one back with `node "/engine/apps/server/assets/music/make-music.mjs" pick "<edit dir>" <its id>`. Say in that note's line what you measured and which take you kept.
- At most two makes in this round, counting the drop check. If a make fails, the music stays as it was: say so, and why, in that note's line of the round.
- A note that is unclear: take the most likely reading. A note that is impossible or goes against the brief: do the closest thing that works.
- A voice note without a transcript: transcribe it with ~/Developer/video-use/.venv/bin/python ~/Developer/video-use/helpers/transcribe.py "<file>" --edit-dir "./edit/review/voice".
- Add a section "## Round 1" at the end of project.md with one line per note: what you changed, or why you did something else.

Finish the edit as a live preview, not a rendered video. The owner watches it in Studio Engine and leaves notes; the final MP4 is rendered only after they approve.
- Build the finish as a HyperFrames composition (§3.5 Mode B), even when every graphic only sits on top of the footage.
- The project is edit/preview/. Its root composition is edit/preview/index.html, with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height and data-duration on the root element.
- Start the root composition's main script with `window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};` (the player loads its runtime after the page's own scripts).
- Everything the composition loads sits inside edit/preview/ and is referenced by a relative path: the baked cut (edit/preview/cut.mp4, §3.5 step 2), music, fonts, GSAP, images and sub-compositions. No absolute paths and no URLs: a browser loads this folder as it is.
- Every video it plays is H.264 in SDR, so a browser can play it. When you crop hard and place clips from the sources (the exception in §3.5 step 2), make H.264 SDR intermediates of those clips inside edit/preview/ first.
- Do not run hyperframes render and do not write edit/final.mp4.
- Self-eval on the composition instead of a render: npx hyperframes lint with 0 errors, snapshots at every cut and at each graphic's payoff (npx hyperframes snapshot), the caption gate (§3.4 step 5) on those snapshots, and the loudness of cut.mp4 with the music under it.
- A graphic that fades or slides out must finish doing so inside its clip: a `class="clip"` element is hidden after data-start + data-duration, so that sum has to be at or after the end of the exit tween. Check a snapshot at the exit.
- Look at the snapshots for what each caption and graphic sits on: over every shot it appears on, it must not cover text, a face or a key object in the picture. If it would, use the nearest clear position (or a stronger caption background) and say so in project.md.
- Record the composition in project.md: where it is, its graphics and their timing.
- Mark the text so Studio Engine can show a font note live: the captions' host (the one with data-track-kind="captions") also carries data-timeline-role="captions"; every title, lower third, callout and end card (the host of its sub-composition, or the element itself when it sits in index.html) carries data-timeline-role="title". If the composition already exists, add the attributes where they are missing. They change nothing in the picture.
- The job is done when edit/preview/index.html passes lint and you have checked the snapshots. Do not leave anything running in the background when you finish.

This run is unattended (Studio Engine): nobody will answer questions, so never ask any. Follow the skill's §0 and decide on judgment. Notes for this machine:
- Setup is already done: ~/Developer/video-use is cloned with its .venv, and the skill is installed at ~/.claude/skills/video-use. Skip the ln -sfn line in §1 (writes under ~/.claude are blocked here); run the rest of §1's checks.
- This is the local Mac, not a cloud container: work directly in ./edit/ and skip §4 (no staging, device_commit_files or SendUserFile).
- The job path contains spaces and may be Hebrew, so always double-quote paths and variables in Bash (`cd "$SH"`, never `cd $SH`). Never cd or write above ./edit/, and if a cd fails, stop instead of running the next command where you are: a stray folder in the client folder or the inbox gets picked up as a new job.
- Read only this folder. The client's style, this job's series (if it has one) and the shared fonts are already copied into edit/style/, edit/series/ and edit/fonts/, so don't open the client's other folders (other jobs, _Style, _Series, _Fonts) or anything else in the inbox. The one exception is the client's _Shared folder (../_Shared/) when brief.md lists its files: copy the ones you use into edit/shared/ and use them from there.
- macOS tools: Bash is bash 3.2 and sed is BSD sed, so in-place edits need sed -i '' (or use the Edit tool). The edit-video skill is at ~/.claude/skills/edit-video.
- iPhone clips: this ffmpeg has no zscale, so render.py's HLG/HDR tone-map fails; make SDR intermediates first (VideoToolbox scale_vt works here). Keep every clip's orientation: a portrait iPhone clip is stored landscape with a rotation (ffprobe -show_entries stream_side_data=rotation shows e.g. -90). ffmpeg applies that rotation to software-decoded frames only, not to hardware frames (-hwaccel_output_format videotoolbox_vld), so after hwdownload add the turn yourself (transpose=clock for -90, transpose=cclock for 90, hflip,vflip for 180) and check that each intermediate has the width and height the source is shown at.
- The ElevenLabs key is in ~/Developer/video-use/.env, where the transcribe helper reads it. Never print it, copy it or pass it on a command line: everything this run prints is logged.
- If you hit a real blocker, finish what does not depend on it, then make the very last line of your final message start with "Blocked:" followed by one plain sentence naming what is missing, for example "Blocked: ffmpeg is not installed (brew install ffmpeg)." Studio Engine shows that sentence to the user as the job's error.
